summary: Palau’s restoration commitments are the most concrete: afforestation and reforestation of degraded land are planned for up to 500 ha by 2040, including 250 ha by 2035, while a separate 120 ha of reforested land is reported without a timeframe; the 500-ha maximum equals about 1.8% of the country’s current 272 km² forest area. Restoration also includes rehabilitating eight closed dump sites by 2030. Under mixed agriculture and conservation measures, Palau targets a 50% increase in land used for taro production, while pursuing sustainable farm improvements, coral and mangrove protection, and coastal restoration. Its conservation strategy seeks 100% sustainable management of the exclusive economic zone. Agricultural measures also introduce biogas at 16 commercial pig farms; because neither taro area nor farm size is reported, these pledges cannot be compared directly with the country’s 96 km² of agricultural land.
